title: Texting rules and fair housing basics
summary: The rules that keep you and your clients safe. This is general training, not legal advice.

lessons.title: Texting and calling rules (TCPA)
lessons.body:
US law protects people from unwanted texts and automatic calls.

- Text only people who **agreed** to texts. RightAlly saves their agreement and the words they saw.
- Texts and automatic calls go out only between **8 am and 9 pm** in the person's own time zone.
- When someone replies **STOP**, never text them again.
- Skip numbers on the **Do Not Call** list.

When in doubt, call the person yourself or send an email.

lessons.title: Fair housing in everyday words
lessons.body:
Treat every client the same, whatever their race, colour, religion, sex, disability, family status or national origin. Many states and cities protect more groups.

- Describe **the home**, not the people you think should live there. Say "three bedrooms near a park", not "perfect for a young family".
- Never steer people toward or away from a neighbourhood.
- Answer questions about schools or crime by pointing to public sources.

RightAlly's **Marketing check** flags risky wording before you post.

questions.q: A lead filled in your form but did not tick the box agreeing to texts. What do you do?
options: Add them to a text campaign
questions.why: Texts need the person's agreement. Call or email instead.

questions.q: What time may automatic texts go out?
questions.why: The quiet hours follow the person's own time zone.
Describe the home, not the people you think should live there.
